#### Why do you use palm oil in your No Stir Peanut Butter and No Stir Almond Butter?
We add a small amount of natural palm oil to help keep the nut oil from separating from the solid part of the nut.

- [Are MaraNatha Nut Butters Kosher?](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#23)
- [What is the Xerces Society?](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#24)

#### Why does the oil separate on top of some of your products?

Oil separation occurs naturally in our non-stabilized nut butters soon after the products are made because we do not put any ingredients in the products to keep the oil from separating from the nut solids. As a result, these products require stirring prior to use.

Please do not drain off the natural oil on top or you will end up with a nut butter that is dry, hard and difficult to spread.

If you don’t want to have to stir your nut butter, we offer MaraNatha No Stir Peanut and Almond Butters, which are ready to use immediately after opening—no stirring required!

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### Why do you use palm oil in your No Stir Peanut Butter and No Stir Almond Butter?

We add a small amount of natural palm oil to help keep the nut oil from separating from the solid part of the nut. Adding the palm oil results in nut butter that does not need to be stirred and spreads more easily.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### How is your palm oil extracted? Is any chemical processing used?

No. Palm oil used in MaraNatha No Stir nut butters is extracted from the fruit or pulp of the palm tree and purified without the use of artificial flavors, artificial colors, or synthetic ingredients.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### Why did you create No Stir Peanut Butter and No Stir Almond Butter?

We created our No Stir nut butters as a response to consumer demand from people who want nut butter that is not hydrogenated, is lightly sweetened and does not have to be stirred.

For those people who prefer fewer ingredients or unsweetened nut butters and don’t mind stirring, we also make single ingredient natural and organic nut butters.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### Why do you add sugar to your No Stir Peanut Butter and No Stir Almond Butters?

A small amount of evaporated cane juice sugar enhances the rich roasted flavor of the nuts, providing a taste experience many consumers prefer.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### How should I store MaraNatha products?

For optimum flavor and ease of use, follow these simple steps: Stir and Refrigerate. Our No-Stir products don’t require stirring prior to refrigeration.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### Do I really need to refrigerate MaraNatha nut butters?

It’s generally best to refrigerate our nut butters. Because they do not contain any artificial preservatives or stabilizers, they can become rancid if left out of refrigeration for an extended period of time and/or exposed to warm temperatures. Unless you have purchased one of our No Stir items, remember to stir your nut butter before you put it in the fridge. Otherwise you’ll have a bit of a challenge on your hands.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### How do I read the date code on your jars?

U.S.date codes are usually listed as day, month, year, (DDMMMYY). For example,  09FEB20 is February 9, 2020.  Canadian date codes are usually listed as year, month, day, YYMMDD 20MA09 is May 9, 2020.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### Do your products ever last beyond the code date?

We guarantee the quality of our products up to the code date, assuming they have been stored correctly.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### Why do some of your products have salt but others don’t?

We consider the judicious use of sea salt to be a highly personal flavor preference. We offer products with salt and without salt.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### What is the difference between your “raw” and “roasted” products?

Raw nut butter products are made from pasteurized almonds, however they do not go through the same heat treatments as the roasted products. Roasted nut butters are baked or heated to produce a desired flavor and/or color prior to grinding.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### Are MaraNatha Nut Butters gluten free?

Yes, our nut butters are certified gluten-free by GFCO.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### Are your Almond Butters peanut-free?

Our Almond butters do not contain peanuts, but currently our Almond and Peanut butters are produced in the same facility using shared equipment.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### Are MaraNatha Nut Butters Kosher?

Yes, they are certified Kosher.

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

#### What is the Xerces Society?

Mission of Xerces Society:

The Xerces Society for Invertebrate Conservation is an international nonprofit organization that protects the natural world through of invertebrates and their habitats. We take our name from the now extinct Xerces Blue butterfly _(Glaucopsyche xerces)_, the first butterfly known to go extinct in North America as a result of human activities.

Learn more at [xerces.org/mission](https://xerces.org/mission).

[Back to top.](https://www.maranathafoods.com/health-facts/nut-butter-faqs/#top)

web.title: Natural peanut butter - My Fearless Kitchen
web.description: The ingredients for this include peanuts, sugar, palm oil, and salt. The palm oil is the stabilizer that keeps the peanut oil from separating.
web.markdown:
[Home](https://www.myfearlesskitchen.com/) » Natural peanut butter

The “regular” peanut butter most of us grew up with had the same consistency from the top of the jar to the bottom. This is because of the addition of vegetable oils, which stabilize the peanut butter so the natural peanut oil does not separate from the peanut paste.

Natural peanut butters are becoming more common in the grocery store. The benefit of these is that the only ingredients are peanuts and salt. The drawback is that without the added vegetable oils, the oil separates from the peanut paste and you need to stir the oil and the paste back together.

The one time I tried natural peanut butter, I made a **giant** mess. Huge. Peanut oil everywhere. And I sort of wrote it off as not worth it.

But, in the spirit of knowledge (and adventure), I tried again. Just so I could write this article.

## Natural peanut butter

Here’s where I started. [Smuckers Natural Peanut Butter](http://www.smuckers.com/products/category.aspx?groupId=2&categoryId=11 "Smuckers Natural Peanut Butter"). The ingredients list includes peanuts and salt. That’s it.

[![smuckers creamy natural label](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20302%20287'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://i0.wp.com/www.myfearlesskitchen.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/smuckers-creamy-natural-label.jpg?ssl=1)

And, as expected, a layer of peanut oil on the top of the peanut butter.

[![smuckers creamy natural top](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20302%20241'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://i0.wp.com/www.myfearlesskitchen.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/smuckers-creamy-natural-top.jpg?ssl=1)

Taking [some advice](http://www.peanutbutterboy.com/peanut-butter-101/# "Peanut Butter Boy"), I dumped the entire jar of peanut butter into a bowl to give it a good mix. Make sure you get everything off the bottom, it tends to get kind of thick at the bottom of the jar, and that’s the part that needs the oil the most!

[![smuckers creamy natural mixed](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20352%20365'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://i0.wp.com/www.myfearlesskitchen.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/smuckers-creamy-natural-mixed.jpg?ssl=1)

Then I put everything back into the original jar. (And made a mess. But not a giant one.)

Natural peanut butter does not need to be refrigerated, but refrigeration will help keep the oil from separating. Refrigeration will also make the peanut butter very thick, and you may need to warm it up a little bit before it spreads easily.

## No-stir natural peanut butter

For those of us who are stir-challenged, there is a variety of natural peanut butter that does not need to be stirred. This is [Skippy’s No-Stir Natural Peanut Butter](http://www.peanutbutter.com/product "Skippy Peanut Butter"). The ingredients for this include peanuts, sugar, palm oil, and salt. The palm oil is the stabilizer that keeps the peanut oil from separating. (Yes, I know using oil to keep oil from separating sounds strange. But that’s how it works.)

[![skippy natural no-stir label](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20302%20318'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://i0.wp.com/www.myfearlesskitchen.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/skippy-natural-no-stir-label.jpg?ssl=1)

Did you notice something strange on the label? This is peanut butter _spread_. Which means that it [contains less than 90% peanuts](https://www.myfearlesskitchen.com/2012/11/13/peanut-butter/ "Peanut butter") (by finished weight). That addition of the palm oil pushes it over the 90% threshold to be able to be called peanut _butter_. I couldn’t find anywhere on the label that does declare the percentage of peanuts it contains.

Here’s the top of the new jar, no oil in sight!

[![skippy natural no-stir top](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20302%20289'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://i0.wp.com/www.myfearlesskitchen.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/skippy-natural-no-stir-top.jpg?ssl=1)

## Comparison

But, how do the two varieties compare?

Here’s a close up of the Smuckers Natural Peanut Butter. It’s got a little bit of a grainy texture, which I absolutely love. While it had a fantastic peanut flavor, it did have just a little bit of an oily feel, and left me with a slight oily taste. I’m sure this will be great on a sandwich, but I won’t be eating this straight out of the jar anytime soon.

[![smuckers creamy natural sample](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20402%20283'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://i0.wp.com/www.myfearlesskitchen.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/smuckers-creamy-natural-sample.jpg?ssl=1)

And the Skippy No-Stir Natural Peanut Butter. This looks a little more like the “regular” peanut butter I’m used to. It didn’t have the strong peanut flavor of the Smuckers, but it also didn’t have the oily feeling.

[![skippy natural no-stir sample](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20502%20256'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://i0.wp.com/www.myfearlesskitchen.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/skippy-natural-no-stir-sample.jpg?ssl=1)

I have to say, taste-wise it’s a bit of a toss up for me. I would probably choose the Smuckers for a sandwich or a smoothie, but the Skippy for snacking on fruit or pretzels (or the occasional dip out of the jar).

## Nutrition

Here are the two nutrition labels for comparison. The Smuckers has more calories per serving, less saturated fat, less sodium, and less sugar. But, frankly, there’s not a very big nutrition difference between the two.

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| **Smuckers Natural Peanut Butter nutrition label** | **Skippy No-Stir Natural Peanut Butter nutrition label** |
| ![smuckers creamy natural nutrition label](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20240%20487'%3E%3C/svg%3E)![smuckers creamy natural ingredients](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20238%2072'%3E%3C/svg%3E) | [![skippy natural no-stir nutrition label](data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg%20xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'%20viewBox='0%200%20250%20357'%3E%3C/svg%3E)](https://i0.wp.com/www.myfearlesskitchen.com/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/skippy-natural-no-stir-nutrition-label.jpg?ssl=1) |

What do you think? Do you already use natural peanut butter? Are you going to try it?

_{I am not endorsing either brand. These were handy at my local grocery store.}_
